chunks: the well that happens to be five cubits from the cesspool, or less or more — can wudu be performed from it? He said: 'Its abhorrence is not due to its proximity or distance; wudu and ghusl may be performed from it as long as the water has not changed.'

key_terms.أَذْرُع: cubits — traditional unit of length, approximately the distance from the elbow to fingertip
key_terms.الْكَنِيف: cesspool/latrine — an outdoor toilet or waste pit adjacent to the well
key_terms.يَتَغَيَّرِ الْمَاءُ: the water changes — alteration in taste, smell, or colour that renders water impure
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: is considered makruh (reprehensible) — a legal category just below haram

ai.seo_question: Can wudu and ghusl be performed from a well located near a cesspool or bathroom?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) addresses a practical jurisprudential question about well water near a cesspool. The Imam rules that the proximity of a well to a toilet facility — whether five cubits, less, or more — does not in itself render the water ritually reprehensible for performing wudu or ghusl. The decisive criterion is whether the water's physical properties (taste, smell, or colour) have changed due to contamination, reflecting the Islamic legal principle that water is ritually pure unless demonstrably altered.
